steps.text: A gift card is a code with money on it. This video shows how to sell gift cards, issue them by hand, follow and change each balance, how buyers pay with them at checkout, and what happens on a refund.
A gift card is a gift that cannot be the wrong size or colour. For a store it is cash up front, and a reason for a friend to become a customer.
Doing it by hand means codes in a spreadsheet, balances nobody trusts, and cards that are spent twice.
A gift card is a code with money on it. A buyer types it at checkout, it pays part or all of the order, and what is left stays on the card.
You can sell gift cards like any product, and issue them by hand, for example to make up for a late delivery.
Selling one: a gift card product holds a price. When an order for it is paid, one card for that amount is issued and emailed to the buyer.
Issuing one by hand: enter an amount, a recipient and, if you like, your own code and an expiry date.
Spending one: the buyer types the code at checkout. It pays like a second way to pay, and tax is worked out on the full price first.
Following one: every card has a page with its balance and an activity list of every change. Open Commerce, Gift cards.
Turning the feature on creates a Gift card content type. Open Content, Content Items, and create a new Gift card.
Give it a title, such as Gift card 50 dollars, and a Price of 50. The price is what each card holds. Publish it, and it is ready to sell like any product.
To show it in the shop, open Commerce, Product Listings, and edit the Shop. Under the product types it lists, tick Gift card, and publish.

chapters.title: Issue a gift card by hand
chapters.subtitle: Amount, code, recipient and expiry

steps.text: Open Commerce, Gift cards, and click Issue gift card. Enter the Amount, and check the Currency, which starts with your checkout currency.
The Code is optional. Leave it blank to have an unguessable sixteen character code made up, or type your own, such as one printed on a physical card.
Fill in the recipient's name and email, an optional expiry date, a message for the email, and a note for the store only, such as why the card was given.
Email the card sends the code to the recipient. Clear it to hand over the code yourself, and click Issue.

chapters.title: A gift card's page
chapters.subtitle: Balance, activity and sending it again

steps.text: The card's page shows its whole code, its balance, when it was issued, and for a bought card, a link to the order. You can change the recipient, the expiry and the note, or clear Enabled to stop the card paying without changing its balance.
Under Change the balance, enter an Amount and a Reason, and click Change balance. A positive amount adds to the card and a negative one takes off it. A reason is required, and is kept with the card.
Activity lists every change, newest first: what it was, the change, and the balance after it. Under Email the card, Send emails the code again, for example when it was lost.

chapters.title: Buy a gift card
chapters.subtitle: A gift card is a product

steps.text: Shoppers find a gift card in the shop and buy it like anything else. It is a digital product, so nothing ships.
When the order is paid, one card is issued for each one bought, and it is emailed to the buyer to pass on. An order paid offline issues its cards turned off, until the money arrives.
On the Payment step, the buyer types the code in the Gift card box and clicks Apply. Dashes, spaces and capital letters do not matter.
The box lists the card by its last four characters, what it pays, and what will be left on it, and the summary shows what is still due now. When cards pay everything, the button reads Place order.
The order, its invoice and its confirmation email show Paid with gift card, and the amount.

chapters.title: Find your gift cards
chapters.subtitle: The list, filters and the order link

steps.text: Commerce, Gift cards lists every card, newest first, with only the last four characters of each code. Search by code, its last four characters, or the recipient's email.
Filter by status: Active, Used up, Expired or Disabled. Each card shows its balance, when it expires, who it is for, and the order it was bought with.
Open a card that was spent at checkout, and its activity shows what was spent, on which order, and what is left.
Refunding an order paid with a gift card puts the money back on the card or wallet first, then on the gift card, and the card's activity shows it.
Canceling or fully refunding an order that bought a card turns the card off, as long as nothing was spent from it.
The money is held for a checkout while the buyer pays the rest, so two buyers cannot spend the same money.
Codes avoid easy to misread characters, and trying many codes in a row is stopped.

chapters.title: Use cases
chapters.subtitle: Four ways to use gift cards

steps.text: Sell cards in the amounts you choose, such as 25, 50 and 100, for the holidays.
Make up for a late delivery with a card issued by hand.
Print your own codes for a physical card in the shop.
Give a prize or a loyalty reward, with an expiry date where the law allows one.
Sell them, issue them, follow every balance, and let buyers spend them at checkout. Thanks for watching.
